MATEX COIN / PROTOCOL-OWNED LIQUIDITY LAB

MATEx Coin.
MGAS handles the gas.

MATEx Coin is the proposed currency and trading asset; MGAS is the gas mechanism. The first local implementation tests a separate ERC-20 representation on Base Sepolia with protocol-owned MATEx/USDC liquidity. It does not launch a native MateX chain.

  1. Start with test assets

    The test coin has 18 decimals, zero initial supply and a 1,000,000-coin test cap. The approved seed is 1,000 tMATEX plus 10 canonical Base Sepolia test USDC. The planned opening marginal quote is 0.01 test USDC; actual reserves determine the observed quote.

  2. Separate trading and gas

    A 0.30% AMM trading fee stays in the pool. MGAS uses the existing Alchemy paymaster to quote smart-wallet actions separately in tMGAS, with the configured 10% service markup. One-time deployments and the initial mint use owner test ETH.

  3. Keep liquidity with the protocol

    Only the protocol treasury adds or removes liquidity. Public two-way swaps use exact inputs, minimum outputs and deadlines. LP shares are nontransferable and include permanently locked minimum-liquidity dust.

  4. Require matching receipts

    Completion requires the exact user operation, pool effects, principal transfers and separate bounded gas collection at a canonical checkpoint. Unknown responses preserve the original tracking ID and never trigger an automatic replay.

71 focused internal checks passed: 14 real-EVM contract tests and 57 wallet/API/server checks. Public Base Sepolia deployments, funded liquidity and MGAS-paid live pool receipts remain pending. The local page is implemented and tested; it is not an independent audit, mainnet market, profitable HFT proof or a token-price guarantee. Existing gas credits and wrapped test tokens are separate assets. Read the implementation and verification scope ↗

SENTINEL / PREVENTIVE SECURITY PREVIEW

See the risk.
Before you approve.

Sentinel is MATEx's opt-in security agent, designed to flag potentially risky Solidity code and onchain contract changes before users approve transactions. It combines source review, contract observations and exact-transaction analysis with clear findings and proposed remediation. Users retain control of their wallets; fixes and protective actions require review.

The first local preview covers owned sources and pinned Arc testnet contracts through a separate five-tool MCP connector. Live polling is opt-in and runs only while its local page is open. No wallet-wide interception, background monitoring service or automatic remediation is enabled. These checks are not an independent audit or a guarantee of preventing exploits. Read the scope and agent workflow ↗

ARC TESTNET / WRAPPED TOKEN PREPARATION

One token locked.
One wrapped token issued.

The local wtMGAS implementation is prepared as a transferable, 1:1 wrapper around the existing Arc testnet tMGAS token. Live deployment verification is pending. No verified deployment, wtMGAS pool, market trades or mainnet release are claimed.

  1. Keep backing in token units

    One tMGAS deposited mints one wtMGAS, with six decimals and zero initial wrapped supply. The underlying token is pinned to 0x28d0369964820248fc3f34c708d6d1d7288dbbbb on Arc testnet, chain 5042002. Direct underlying donations create surplus backing without minting claims.

  2. Let the current holder redeem

    wtMGAS supports standard token transfers. Whoever holds it can burn an amount to reclaim the same amount of tMGAS. Transferring wtMGAS also transfers that redemption claim. This is token redemption, not a USDC peg, cash-out or resale guarantee.

  3. Review each exact wallet action

    The local page prepares deployment, an exact tMGAS allowance, wrapping and unwrapping for separate human MetaMask review. The wallet pays native Arc test-USDC network fees. Wrapping is not gasless, and it does not automatically create a trading venue or funded liquidity.

  4. Check supply against backing

    The wrapper has no administrator mint, upgrade or recovery withdrawal. Backing must cover wrapped supply; the existing underlying tMGAS token still has its owner-controlled minting. Balances, backing, supply and surplus are checked together at a block checkpoint.

The local wallet page now uses explicit EIP-6963 MetaMask selection, with a visibly unverified legacy fallback. Read-only provider diagnostics check account access, network, block, latest nonce and native balance. Safe request stages and error categories remain distinct from transaction confirmation. Inputs are captured before the busy render can overwrite a selected wallet, address, acknowledgement or reconciliation hash.

Internal validation passed eight isolated EVM tests, twenty-nine controller tests and eighteen wallet tests (55 focused checks). Same-nonce recovery retains up to three reviewed candidates. At that limit, an explicit human review can reopen the exact saved candidate with its nonce, gas, gas price and maximum fee unchanged. No request is sent automatically. Internal review identifiers are not transaction hashes. These checks are not an independent audit, a verified live wallet prompt or a confirmed deployment. Live deployment verification remains pending. Arc tMGAS and wtMGAS remain separate from Base-funded service credits; no bridge, shared gas dispatch or new MCP wrapping tools are enabled by this addition.

MATEX TRADING / ACTUAL USDC DENOMINATION

Research SOL.
Account in USDC.

The local lab now separates the original price/funding proxy from native Binance SOLUSDC research. Eight focused daily-momentum cases bring the catalogue to 28; the Python research MCP still exposes eleven tools. Quote, collateral and settlement asset identities remain explicit.

  1. Use native market inputs

    Binance SOLUSDC trades, marks and published funding share one actual USDC-margined contract. The new source cannot silently fall back to SOLUSDT or Hyperliquid history.

  2. Respect the settlement calendar

    The engine charges whole published interval rates only at native settlements. Stress and adverse fallback rates scale by interval duration. Price levels round to the contract tick. Legacy hourly paths and prior frozen studies retain their behavior.

  3. Inspect improvement and failure together

    A funding-filter case grew a continuous baseline account from 20 to 25.7790 USDC, with five positive marked period changes. It still failed one fresh window and fell to 17.0871 under stress. The validation-selected case remained insufficiently sampled.

  4. Keep Circle alignment precise

    USDC is the native quote, collateral and settlement denomination in this research source. This addition is not a new Circle API integration, Circle endorsement or verified live trade. Existing Arc report payments remain a separate service rail.

Fees and maintenance include explicit research assumptions; exact venue liquidation and historical fee/bracket changes are not reconstructed. The site publishes data provenance, all 96 comparisons and full review exports. Inspect the native-USDC study ↗

MATEX TRADING / LEVERAGED SIMULATION

Account for leverage.
Keep every failure.

The local Perps Research lab and two additional MateX MCP tools simulate ETH/SOL long and short positions with $20 collateral, fees on full notional, hourly funding, minimum orders and mark-based isolated liquidation. Ten hypotheses are fixed before evaluation.

  1. Respect event timing

    Completed signals enter at the next open. Funding applies only at settlement while a position is open; it cannot change an earlier stopped trade. Known open exits precede later mark extremes.

  2. Keep collateral isolated

    The conservative liquidation proxy loses remaining position collateral, preserving unrelated free balance. Quantity rounding, the $10 opening minimum, a $150 notional cap and per-trade risk constrain exposure even at higher leverage.

  3. Separate selection from later outcomes

    All ten candidates are published at 5× across five windows. Only the validation-selected candidate receives 2×/5×/10×/20× and adverse-cost comparisons. Neither asset passed the positive development-and-validation screen; the later 15-day check also lost for both fallbacks.

  4. Expose useful evidence to agents

    matex_get_perps_research describes coverage and limits. matex_start_perps_backtest starts a bounded job; matex_get_job returns results. Dashboard/MCP histories are compacted with explicit counts; CLI exports retain complete logs. No wallet or exchange-order capability is added.

Binance USD-M prices and marks plus Hyperliquid funding form a mixed-venue proxy, not exact venue execution. Funding oracle price, current margin tiers, conservative backstop loss and close-marked drawdown are assumptions. Three day-series per asset use official REST repairs with response hashes; these are distinguished from archive checksum verification. Inspect the complete public study ↗

MATEX TRADING / RELIABLE RESEARCH INPUTS

Choose the market.
Keep the assumptions visible.

The local trading dashboard and its separate eleven-tool research MCP now accept BTC, ETH or SOL, starting capital and per-fill slippage. This is separate from the 15-tool MATEx GAS preview and four-tool managed report connector.

  1. Use the actual selected market

    Source-specific symbols and separate candle caches carry the chosen BTC, ETH or SOL market into backtests, rolling walk-forward tests and execution comparisons. Sample and generated data keep their simulation labels.

  2. Size the simulated account honestly

    The starting-capital control, including a 20-unit preset, reaches actual broker sizing. New journal entries and exports retain market and effective cost settings. Fee and slippage assumptions remain visible; buy-and-hold is labelled as a gross benchmark.

  3. Recover paper candles in order

    After a polling interruption, a paper account processes each available unseen closed candle using only the history available then and saves each step. Missing checkpoint history, changed checkpoint prices and detected cadence gaps block the batch. A legacy single-bar feed may still need cadence information.

  4. Keep the proof in scope

    Running API checks used three months of real four-hour ETH and SOL candles with 20-unit simulation accounts, plus walk-forward and cost-comparison checks. These are internal functional checks, not a profitable-strategy selection, adoption or live execution proof.

The original research remains fractional spot simulation at 1×. The separate leveraged-perpetual model is documented below; its venue proxies and limits remain explicit. Paper recovery does not replay actual exchange orders, and closed-candle stops do not establish intrabar execution. The private platform source remains outside this website repository.

NEW MANAGED REPORT WORKFLOW

Policies before payments.
Reports with evidence.

The managed connector is a separate four-tool local stdio preview. It does not change the existing 15-tool keyless connector or three-skill catalog.

  1. Approve the agent’s boundaries

    In the local Control Center, the buyer’s owner wallet reviews the exact policy and signs its activation. Limits use six-decimal USDC service prices and UTC day/week windows. The policy allows specific report services, report networks and seller addresses.

  2. Connect the registered agent privately

    Reveal or copy its connection key only for a trusted local MCP client. The server stores a hash. Private credentials stay in the client environment and out of model prompts, URLs and tool results. A connection key cannot change the owner’s policy or sign a wallet action.

  3. Reserve one exact report

    The agent checks its policy and catalog, then creates one request with a stable key, exact price maximum and frozen report input. The backend enforces the per-request and remaining daily/weekly budgets before authorization. The report network is distinct from the fixed Arc payment network.

  4. Verify payment, then deliver

    The buyer signs an exact USDC authorization; the seller separately reviews Circle settlement. A matching canonical payment receipt precedes report execution. The returned delivery receipt binds the original input, result hash and payment. Uncertain payments retain their budget hold and are never automatically resent.

US / USD · FUNDING PREVIEW

Fund with clear boundaries.
Prove what arrived.

The local Funding hub has an installed Circle Onramp Kit 1.0.8 sandbox integration. A live provider session and verified deposit remain to be demonstrated. This public page provides documentation; it does not open a payment session.

  1. Choose the right environment

    The embedded flow is sandbox only and moves no real funds. The official Arc Portal is a separate external real-money handoff. It does not fund the current MATEx testnet token or credit accounts.

  2. Confirm wallet ownership

    The local hub requires an EIP-191 wallet-ownership proof before issuing a sandbox session. It uses a separate server-only sandbox credential and limits the widget to USDC and Arc. This proof does not authorize a purchase, transfer or agent spending.

  3. Let the provider determine eligibility

    Providers independently check the user's actual US state, payment method, identity and applicable business onboarding. Targeting US/USD does not establish eligibility. Provider fees and network costs are separate from MATEx service markup.

  4. Verify the deposit separately

    Widget callbacks alone do not prove settlement. Sandbox uses dummy details only; its bank-transfer test currently delivers test tokens only on Ethereum. An Arc testnet deposit must not be inferred from that result.

◈

Cash-out is a separate planned route.

Direct Arc off-ramp support is unverified. The proposed route is separately owner-reviewed CCTP bridging from Arc USDC to Base USDC, followed by eligible Coinbase USD checkout. Neither route is implemented or enabled here. The existing one-way tMGAS converter does not provide a redemption guarantee.

The MATEx workspace remains a local testnet preview. No real-money deposit, mainnet transaction, cash-out or redemption has been demonstrated by this integration. The sandbox form must never receive real identity or payment details.

FOR DEVELOPERS WITH WORKSPACE ACCESS

Bring your own client.
Keep approval with you.

  1. Start the local workspace

    Use the project’s local operator instructions and Node.js 22 or later. The public website repository contains this site and research downloads; it does not contain the private payment backend or an installable agent service.

  2. Connect the preview through stdio

    In the local Agents section, copy the generated MCP configuration into your own MCP-compatible client. Use its separate command and arguments fields. A web page URL is not the stdio MCP connection.

  3. Discover, then request

    List the connector’s actual tools and read the relevant registry skill. For an Arc token purchase, quote the exact amount, keep one request key and return the review page to the owner. A quote or request does not authorize spending.

  4. Review in MetaMask, then inspect evidence

    The owner approves the exact allowance and purchase separately. Poll the original request ID. Report success only when the state is confirmed and its receipt is verified. An uncertain submission keeps its existing intent; it is not automatically resent.

Use Solana mode: select Solana Devnet in the local copilot, choose the public Solana address to inspect, then ask for its balances or missing setup steps. The three tools are status, balances and setup checklist. This mode only reads; it cannot prepare, sign or send a transaction.

◈

One token vision. Explicit accounting today.

Arc USDC conversion, Circle Facilitator checkout and Base-funded service credits are separate flows. Arc native USDC uses 18 decimals; its ERC-20 interface uses six and represents the same balance. The Arc tMGAS purchase has no 10% sale markup; service pricing and network fees are disclosed separately.
